title: Mexico with Ramon Mantoya's band and Acapulco
summary: Edison recalls the Mexico engagement, the former Lunceford trombonist who led the band, and playing Acapulco.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Oh, yes, just about 18. But the fellow who had the band, he was a former trombone player with Jimmy Lunceford. He was a Mexican fellow called Raymond Toya.
M-a-n-t-o-y-a. Ramon Mantoya. And he was a fantastic trumpet player. He played with Jimmy Lunceford, I guess, about a couple years.
In the later years of JImmy?
Oh, yeah, that's after Trummy and Ray and Ray Bolds, and what was his name, Trombone player?

Yes. Well, it was after that era. He'd begun -- they guys had begun to drift away, you know. Like Willie Smith had gone, Crawford, you know. And that was the tail end of Jimmy Lunceford days, you know. And stayed down there six months. Went to Acapulco and played at a club called the La Perlo, that was owned by -- oh, he was married to Hedy Lamarr. He's still there. In fact, I saw him down there with Sammy Davis last -- about a year ago when Sammy had a show. We went down there and did a series of shows on the beach in Acapulco.
